entities.summary:
Luis Julian de Milà y de Borja was a cardinal of the Catholic Church who played a pivotal role in shaping the Counter-Reformation during the tumultuous early 16th century. Born into the powerful Della Rovere family, he rose through the ranks to become Pope Julius II's close confidant and chief advisor.

As a key figure in the papacy, de Milà y de Borja orchestrated the execution of heretics, promoted the arts, and expanded the Church's influence across Europe. His tenure as cardinal coincided with significant events such as the Sack of Rome in 1527 and the Protestant Reformation's early stages.

De Milà y de Borja's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped establish the Jesuits and influenced the development of Catholic dogma during the Council of Trent. His impact on the Church's stance on faith, art, and governance left a lasting impression on Western history.

The cardinal's remarkable life was marked by both incredible achievements and personal struggles. Despite his formidable position, de Milà y de Borja struggled with depression and faced opposition from within the Church due to his perceived nepotism and favoritism towards certain factions.
